tests.name: strings
tests.description: The String Manipulation functions (indexOf, lastIndexOf, substring, startsWith, endsWith, contains, upper, lower, replace, matches, matchesFull, replaceMatches, length, toChars), the Additional String Functions (encode, decode, escape, unescape, trim, split, join), + on strings and the & operator, Unicode characters as the text counts them, and the FHIR primitive types that reach these functions as System.String. Leaves out what the text does not settle: an empty regular expression, the syntax of a match group and of a substitution's reference to it, named or numbered (including the worked date example of replaceMatches, whose output the text does not state), how . and character classes treat characters outside the BMP, the m flag in matchesFull, invalid flags or an invalid regular expression in replaceMatches, overlapping instances in replace, an empty pattern on an empty string, an empty separator or a separator at either end in split, an empty separator in join, non-String items in join and &, more than one input item, or a non-String input item, to the Additional String Functions, a call to encode, decode, escape or unescape that omits its required format or target, unknown formats and malformed input to encode and decode, which HTML entities escape writes, JSON escapes other than the double quote, the backslash and the line feed, language-specific case mappings, Unicode normalization in comparisons, a non-String argument that 2.0.0 could convert explicitly, and a lone surrogate escape.

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-001

group.source: The functions in this section operate on collections with a single item. If there is more than one item, or an item that is not a String, the evaluation of the expression will end and signal an error to the calling environment.

group.source: The evaluation engine will automatically convert the value of FHIR types representing primitives to FHIRPath types when they are used in expressions according to the following mapping:
FHIR.string, FHIR.uri, FHIR.code, FHIR.oid, FHIR.id, FHIR.uuid, FHIR.sid, FHIR.markdown, FHIR.base64Binary

group.description: A FHIR date maps to a date/time type, not System.String, so a String Manipulation function on it signals an error

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-005
group.description: The 3.0.0 worked example: select() applies substring(0, 1) to each given name in turn (2.0.0's version of the example writes substring(0), which does not return the first character its prose promises)
group.source: To use these functions over a collection with multiple items, one may use filters like `where()` and `select()`:
Patient.name.given.select(substring(0, 1)) // returns a collection containing the first character of all the given names for a patient

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-006
group.description: A collection of more than one item given as an argument that expects a single value signals an error, in every string function (lastIndexOf and matchesFull are 3.0.0 only)
group.source: If the function expects the argument passed to a parameter to be a single value (e.g. `startsWith(prefix: String)`) and it is passed an argument that evaluates to a collection with multiple items, or to a collection with an item that is not of the required type (or cannot be converted to the required type), the evaluation of the expression will end and an error will be signaled to the calling environment.

If a function expects the argument passed to a parameter to be a single value (e.g. `startsWith(prefix: String)`) and it is passed an argument that evaluates to a collection with multiple items, or to a collection with an item that is not of the required type (or cannot be converted to the required type), the evaluation of the expression will end and an error will be signaled to the calling environment.
In general, when a collection is passed as an argument to a function or operator that expects a single item as input, the collection is implicitly converted to a singleton as follows:
The evaluation will end and signal an error to the calling environment

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-014
group.description: substring returns the part of the string from a 0-based start, at most length characters if length is given, and only the remaining characters if fewer remain
group.source: Returns the part of the string starting at position `start` (zero-based). If `length` is given, will return at most `length` number of characters from the input string.
If there are less remaining characters in the string than indicated by `length`, the function returns just the remaining characters.
Returns the part of the string starting at position `start` (zero-based). If `length` is given, will return at most `length` number of characters from the input string.

'abcdefg'.substring(1, 2) // 'bc'
'abcdefg'.substring(6, 2) // 'g'

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-015
group.description: substring is empty when start lies outside the string: at or past its length, or negative
group.source: If `start` lies outside the length of the string, the function returns empty (`{ }`).

If `start` lies outside, or equal to, the length of the string, the function returns empty (`{ }`).
'abcdefg'.substring(-1, 1) // { } (start position is outside the string,
'abcdefg'.substring(-1, -1) // { } (start position is outside the string)
''.substring(0) // { } (start position is outside the string)

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-058
group.description: A \uXXXX escape writes one UTF-16 code unit, and a valid surrogate pair written as two escapes is the single character it encodes (the pair rule is 3.0.0's)
group.source: Unicode character, where XXXX is the hexadecimal representation of the character

When parsing string literals, `\uXXXX` escape sequences represent [UTF-16](https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode16.0.0/core-spec/chapter-3/#G31699) code units; valid surrogate pairs are combined to form a single Unicode scalar value.

After processing escapes, a FHIRPath string is defined as a sequence of Unicode scalar values, which are referred to elsewhere in this specification as `characters` (for example, in [toChars()](#tochars--collection)).

group.description: + on two strings concatenates the right operand to the end of the left one

group.description: + on strings is empty when either operand is empty
group.source: As with the other operators, the math operators will return an empty collection if one or both of the operands are empty.

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-085
group.description: + between a string and a number signals an error: neither converts implicitly to the other
group.source: The math operators require each operand to be a single element. Both operands must be of the same type, or of compatible types according to the rules for implicit conversion. Each operator below specifies which types are supported.
If there is more than one item, or an incompatible item, the evaluation of the expression will end and signal an error to the calling environment.

group.name: REQ-STRINGS-086
group.description: + on strings signals an error when an operand has more than one item, as the worked example of singleton evaluation shows
group.source: If there is more than one item, or an incompatible item, the evaluation of the expression will end and signal an error to the calling environment.
Patient.name.family + ', ' + Patient.name.given

However, if the `Patient` has multiple `name` elements, or the single name has multiple `given` elements, then it's ambiguous which of the elements should be used as the input to the `+` operator, and the result is an error.
